19->17 (band=normal)
A 7-year-old boy with sickle cell disease is brought into the clinic by his mother for knee and hip pain.
The child has been admitted several times in the past for pain crises managed with fluids and

hydromorphone. He started complaining of worsening hip pain over the last several days and now
walks with a limp. His temperature is 99.1°F (36.6°C), blood pressure is 82/58 mmHg, pulse is 62/min,
respirations are 17/min, and oxygen saturation is 99% on room air. On physical exam, the hip appears
normal and is cool to the touch. There is decreased range of motion at the hip and pain with
ambulation. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management? Answer Choices:
(A) CT scan of the pelvis (B) Physical therapy and stretching exercises (C) Ultrasound of the hip (D)
Radiograph (E) Bone scintigraphy (F) Arthrocentesis (G) Ibuprofen and acetaminophen (H) MRI of the
hip (I) Blood cultures and antibiotics (J) Observation and follow-up in 2 weeks
 A. Observation and follow-up in 2 weeks
B. Physical therapy and stretching exercises
C. Ultrasound of the hip
D. Radiograph
E. Blood cultures and antibiotics
F. Ibuprofen and acetaminophen
G. Bone scintigraphy
H. MRI of the hip
I. Arthrocentesis
J. CT scan of the pelvis
